cards.b: One of four titles: two descriptive, two narrative. 350-450 words.
40: 16 content and structure + 24 style and accuracy.
About 10 min plan, 40 min write, 10 min check.
Create a picture and atmosphere, not tell what happens next.
Drifting into narrative with a plot, which limits content and structure marks.
Original and absorbing, well-chosen detail, deliberate structure, consistent atmosphere.
Precise, ambitious vocabulary used correctly, varied sentences for effect, almost error-free.
Wide panorama to mid-shot to close-up on a telling detail, then wide again.
Same place at dawn, noon and night, or before and after an event.
The observer moves through the place; each paragraph is a new area.
End by echoing the opening image, changed.
Use sound, smell, touch, temperature and taste, not just sight.
Giving human qualities to non-human things, e.g. 'the gate groaned'.
The setting or weather reflects the mood.
Cliches, lists of adjectives, repetitive openings ('I see...'), misused ambitious words.

gaps.s: Descriptive writing aims to create a picture and ___.

Style and accuracy is worth ___ marks.

short.q: Explain how a descriptive title differs from a narrative one. [2]
short.model: Descriptive writing focuses on atmosphere and detail. Narrative tells a story with plot and resolution.

short.q: State two features of top-level content and structure. [2]
short.model: Original and absorbing detail, and a clear deliberate structure.

short.q: Give two techniques that score in descriptive writing. [2]
short.model: Sensory detail beyond sight and fresh imagery such as similes or metaphors.
Cliches such as 'as quiet as a mouse' and lists of adjectives.
Describe the same place at different times, such as dawn, noon and night, or before and after an event.
